@graph.headline: Building Privacy-First AI Transparency: The Agent Feed Architecture
@graph.description: Architecture for transparent, privacy-first agent logging: how to monitor autonomous agents without exposing confidential customer data.
@graph.keywords: agent observability, privacy first ai, agent logging architecture, ai transparency, secure llm audit
@graph.abstract: Deploying autonomous agents into business operations requires radical visibility without compromising user privacy. An agent feed architecture captures step-by-step reasoning trajectories, tool invocations, and environmental feedback while automatically scrubbing personally identifiable information and confidential secrets before telemetry reaches monitoring dashboards or shared engineering team channels.

acceptedAnswer.text: A chronological, structured stream of agent decisions, actions, tool executions, and state transitions recorded during task completion.

mainEntity.name: How do you protect sensitive data in agent logs?

acceptedAnswer.text: By using client-side regex and named-entity recognition sanitizers that redact emails, phone numbers, and API tokens before persistent storage.

mainEntity.name: Why is explainability critical in agent systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: When an agent makes an erroneous decision, full trajectory replay is essential to isolate whether the failure stemmed from prompt ambiguity, bad tool input, or model hallucination.

mainEntity.name: Can agent feeds be exported for compliance audits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Structured JSONL logs with cryptographic hash chains provide immutable proof of compliance for regulated enterprise operations.

mainEntity.name: What open-source tools support agent feed telemetry?

acceptedAnswer.text: OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, and lightweight custom event loggers provide structured telemetry without proprietary lock-in.
